title: cascade-strand-attn-kernel-with-interleaved-rotary-rematerialization-and-continuous-batching-hints
author: Arjun Menon
release_notes: Introduces a new CascadeStrand attention kernel with interleaved rotary rematerialization and scheduler hints to improve latency and throughput across mid-to-long sequence workloads. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via config flag. Recommended for quantized and mixed-precision workloads.
description: Summary: Implements the CascadeStrand attention kernel — a vectorized, strided-tiling attention path that interleaves rotary rematerialization with fused q/k/v transforms and a lightweight async-KV eviction hint for continuous-batching workloads. Motivation: latency and tail QPS for mid-long sequences (512-8192) showed uneven performance across our current kernel choices. Existing fused kernels excel at short sequences but suffer from memory blowups and KV contention on continuous-batching streams. CascadeStrand bridges the gap by: 1) tiling sequences into adaptive strands that preserve cache locality, 2) rematerializing rotary embeddings only at tile boundaries (reduces local memory and kernel register pressure), and 3) exposing scheduler hints so the continuous-batcher can pipeline strands across GPUs without blocking hot KV slots. High-level changes: - New kernel: src/runtime/attn/cascade_strand_kernel.cu (vectorized strided GEMM + tiled rotary remat loop). - Scheduler hooks: src/runtime/scheduler/strand_hints.{cpp,h} to propagate per-request strand granularity and preferred batch packing. - KV cache: kv_cache/async_eviction.h adds lightweight eviction hint metadata (not automatic eviction) used by dedicated and hosted modes. - Python bindings and opt-in flag: python/redwood/runtime/experimental.py to enable cascade-strand and runtime config keys. - Tests and benchmarks: tests/attn/cascade_strand_unit_test.py, bench/attn_cascade_stream.py. Commits (summary): - a1d3f7: initial cascade-strand kernel prototype and smoke tests. - b5f2c9: fused qkv transform and rotary remat loop, vectorized loads. - d2e8ab: scheduler hint APIs and continuous-batcher integration. - f7c3e1: microbenchmarks, regressions fixed, CI optimizations. Files touched (high-level): - src/runtime/attn/cascade_strand_kernel.cu - src/runtime/attn/kernel_utils.h - src/runtime/scheduler/strand_hints.cpp - src/runtime/scheduler/strand_hints.h - src/kv/kv_cache.cpp - src/kv/async_eviction.h - python/redwood/runtime/experimental.py - tests/attn/cascade_strand_unit_test.py - bench/attn_cascade_stream.py - docs/ops/cascade_strand.md - examples/serve/cascade_example.yaml - build/CMakeLists.txt Benchmarks: - Short seqs (<=128): ~+2% latency vs current fused path (within noise). - Medium seqs (512-2048): ~-22% median latency, -31% p95 compared to unified-fused kernel. - Long seqs (4096-8192): ~-14% median latency, p95 roughly parity but with 40% lower memory peaks on same batch sizes. - Throughput: up to +18% tokens/sec for continuous-batch microbench scenario (mixed lengths). Regression matrix: ran against models gpt-small/gpt-medium/llama-7B, FP16 and 8-bit postquant. No functional regressions found on unit tests; numerical deltas within acceptable tolerance. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_cascade_strand`. Canary rollout to dedicated clusters in eu-west-1, then opt-in for hosted customers with heavy mid-long workloads. Continuous-batcher will default to previous packing logic until the scheduler hint is enabled. Testing: - Unit tests added to validate rematerialization correctness and strand packing. - Stress test harness simulating long-lived streams with KV churn (bench/attn_cascade_stream.py). - CI: GPU integration tests (cuda-12.1) and macOS CPU smoke. Performance CI includes a new microbench with trending. Review conversation: "Sasha Kim (reviewer): Nice direction. Two asks: (1) can you reduce the register footprint by moving some accumulators to shared memory for older Ampere cards? (2) please add an explicit fallback path when rematerialization is disabled at runtime." "Author (Arjun): Addressed: moved accumulation into shared buffer for legacy SMs (commit d2e8ab) and added runtime check to fall back to unified-fused kernel if remat is disabled (commit f7c3e1)." "Leah Chen (reviewer): Bench numbers look promising. Can you add more deterministic unit tests around boundary tile sizes and odd-length sequences?" "Author: Added tests for tile boundary conditions and odd-length handling (tests/attn/cascade_strand_unit_test.py)." "Ravi Patel (approver): Approve after resolving CI flakiness on the bench runner." CI notes and reruns: initial GPU perf CI had noisy outliers; re-ran microbench with pinned allocation strategy and all checks passed. Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main by Leah Chen after approvals and a final perf smoke. Impact and next steps: - Ops: add `enable_cascade_strand` toggle in console feature flags and include metric dashboards to track latent KV eviction hints and strand packing efficiency. - Research: explore hybridizing with dynamic quantized GEMM paths to squeeze more throughput for 8-bit workloads. - Follow-ups: auto-eviction heuristics for KV (decoupled from this PR) and cross-GPU strand pipelining for multi-GPU per-request execution. Related: ENG-6421 (scheduler improvements), ENG-6533 (KV eviction telemetry). References: internal design doc https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-6421/cascade-strand-design, benchmark outputs in bench/outputs/cascade_2026-01.tar.gz.
